affectedPublicSurfaces: demo.app-juli.com — the release path gains a candidate stage; a release that fails verification never reaches a visitor

candidateVerificationJourney.restrictedRoute: the candidate binds a locally-bound port on the server and is reachable only from the server itself; no nginx upstream, DNS record, or firewall rule exposes it, and the live instance is never touched while it runs

journeys.name: healthy-candidate-proceeds
assertions: the migration gate from #834 runs and accepts before the candidate starts
the candidate starts from the CI artifact placed in the release directory, compiling nothing
the verification harness from #833 passes against the candidate: every referenced stylesheet and script is 2xx with a real body, and core API paths match on shape
only then does the existing cutover proceed

journeys.name: candidate-fails-readiness
assertions: the previously live version is still serving, unmodified, and its process was never restarted

journeys.name: candidate-serves-a-page-with-a-missing-asset
assertions: the harness names the failing asset URL
the candidate is stopped and the deploy exits non-zero
the live instance is untouched — this is the exact failure the slice exists to keep off the public site

journeys.name: candidate-fails-an-api-path
assertions: a healthy process with a broken route fails verification on response shape, not status
the candidate is stopped and the deploy exits non-zero

journeys.name: migration-gate-refuses
journeys.entryUrl: the deploy with a pending destructive migration
assertions: no candidate is started at all
the deploy exits non-zero naming the offending change

migrationCompatibility.notes: The slice introduces no migration of its own. It wires the #834 gate so that migrations are applied before any candidate starts, making ordering deterministic. Migrations are never automatically reverted.

rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: the existing rollback-demo-release.sh path is unchanged by this slice; automatic post-cutover rollback is #840

doNotInfer: zero-downtime or graceful cutover — deliberately out of scope; on success the existing cutover is acceptable and #839 makes it graceful
post-cutover checks or automatic rollback — that is #840
paired slots for the API or landing — that is #843
a single combined deploy command or release record — that is #844
changing nginx upstreams, DNS, or TLS
browser-level styling or interactivity assertions on the server; those run in CI per #837
